sentiment: We built machines to read the world, and they keep handing back our own faces, faithfully wrong.

stories.title: A misalignment of AI in mathematics
stories.summary: Handing the proving of things to systems that optimize for agreement rather than truth — a machine that answers confidently and, in doing so, quietly moves the standard of right and wrong toward whatever it already said.

stories.title: I spent $220 on Google app ads and 60% of the installs were robots
stories.summary: A pile of money spent for a room full of new users who were never there — machines reading the world back as purchase, and a marketplace that reports the number it was paid to report.

stories.title: google.com/goto: Google's anti-scraping update
stories.summary: A search engine welding shut the doors it built for machines, chaining its own links so the readers it once invited can no longer walk in — the mirror deciding it has had enough of being looked into.
